title: DistributedLocallySmoothGrowth.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Each fᵢ is convex and differentiable on all of ℝᵈ with an Lᵢ-Lipschitz gradient, where Lᵢ ≥ 0. The mean F is convex and its gradient satisfies the public Lipschitz bound max(μ, maxᵢ Lᵢ).

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: Minimize F(x) = (1/n)∑ᵢ fᵢ(x) over ℝᵈ, with n ≥ 1 and one local objective per computing worker.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, Point, Functions and objective. LongTails/Setups/DistributedLocallySmoothGrowth.lean, aggregate and spec.Instance.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: At x, worker i returns gᵢ(x,ξ) with mean ∇fᵢ(x). Completed queries use successive samples from that worker’s IID stream with law νᵢ. The streams are independent across workers. All setup parameters are public, including x₀, the Lᵢ, μ, ρ, R, σ, ε and the timing parameters. The local functions, gradient estimators and sampling laws are instance or oracle data.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedLocallySmoothGrowth.lean, Params, spec.Public and spec.publicInput. LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID. LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean, IsStochasticGradient. LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, computation.

distinctive_assumptions.label: gradient_similarity
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x, (1/n)∑ᵢ ‖∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ ρ‖∇F(x)‖², with ρ ≥ 1. This bounds heterogeneity among the local mean gradients. At every minimizer of F, all local mean gradients vanish, while individual stochastic replies can still have positive variance.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedLocallySmoothGrowth.lean, aggregate and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, spec.valid and spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every worker i and point x, Eξ‖gᵢ(x,ξ)−∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ σ² with σ ≥ 0. This bound also applies at minimizers.

distinctive_assumptions.label: quadratic_growth
distinctive_assumptions.details: For S = argmin F, there exists z ∈ S with ‖x₀−z‖ ≤ R, and F(x)−F(z) ≥ (μ/2)dist(x,S)² for every x, with μ > 0 and R ≥ 0. S may have multiple points.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, solutions, spec.valid and spec.admissible, applied by LongTails/Setups/DistributedLocallySmoothGrowth.lean, aggregate and spec.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The query points, local gradient replies and output belong to ℝᵈ with the Euclidean norm, for public d ∈ ℕ.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, Params.d, Point, spec.ComputeQuery, spec.ComputeReply and spec.Output. LongTails/Setups/DistributedLocallySmoothGrowth.lean, aggregate and Point.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Elapsed time is measured on a star with a hub and n computing workers. Worker i takes hᵢ > 0 per completed gradient and can have one evaluation pending. A directed hub–worker link carries one pending message at a time. Sending k payload bits costs ℓ + b(k+64), with ℓ,b ≥ 0. Distinct directed links and worker computations can operate concurrently.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, computation, communication and system. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, clockBits, step and TimedConvergence.

accuracy.label: distance_to_solution
accuracy.details: At the prescribed elapsed-time deadline, the algorithm returns one point X from its designated root. The error is dist(X,argmin F)².
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedLocallySmoothGrowth.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, solutions and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, execute.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: X must be measurable, its squared distance to the solution set must be integrable, and E[dist(X,argmin F)²] ≤ ε for ε > 0 under the product law of algorithm and oracle seeds. Execution must have finitely many events almost surely up to the deadline.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law, FiniteEvents and TimedConvergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines quadratic growth of the mean objective, a strong-growth bound on local mean gradients, and persistent within-worker sampling noise. Its performance criterion charges heterogeneous computation times, message latency and transmitted bits on concurrent star links.

descriptionHtml:
Distributed Minimization Under Strong Growth

We minimize the mean of n≥1 smooth convex functions on Rd, where d is a nonnegative integer. The mean has quadratic growth away from its minimizer set, and the average squared norm of the local gradients is bounded by a multiple of the squared norm of the mean gradient. A given starting point lies within a prescribed radius of a minimizer. On a star network, each worker returns an unbiased local stochastic gradient with bounded variance using an independent sample stream. Given ε>0, the goal is a measurable output whose expected squared Euclidean distance to the minimizer set is at most ε by an elapsed-time deadline.

Write fi:Rd→R for the objective at worker i∈{1,…,n} and define F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x). The optimization problem is minx∈RdF(x). Let S=argminx∈RdF(x) and write dist(x,S)=infz∈S∥x−z∥, using the Euclidean norm throughout.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Local and mean smoothness). Each fi is convex and differentiable on Rd. With local constants Li≥0 and quadratic growth parameter μ>0, set L=max{μ,max1≤i≤nLi}. For all x,y∈Rd, ∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥≤Li∥x−y∥(1≤i≤n),∥∇F(x)−∇F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Strong growth of local gradients). For some ρ≥1 and every x∈Rd, 1n∑i=1n∥∇fi(x)∥2≤ρ∥∇F(x)∥2.

Assumption 3 (Quadratic growth and initial distance). For the given x0∈Rd and R≥0, there exists x⋆∈S such that ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R and F(x)−F(x⋆)≥μ2dist(x,S)2(x∈Rd).

Assumption 4 (Local stochastic gradients). On a common measurable sample space Ω, worker i has a stream of measurable, independent samples (ξi,k)k≥0 with common law νi. The streams are mutually independent, and the algorithm’s randomness is independent of the entire sample array. At its kth completed evaluation, counting from zero, worker i returns the query point x∈Rd and gi(x,ξi,k), where gi:Rd×Ω→Rd is jointly measurable. For every i and x, the gradient estimate is Bochner integrable and its squared error is integrable under νi. For a common σ≥0, they satisfy Eξ∼νi[gi(x,ξ)]=∇fi(x),Eξ∼νi[∥gi(x,ξ)−∇fi(x)∥2]≤σ2.

The star has one central communication node and n computing workers. Worker i takes hi>0 time per evaluation. It can abort a pending evaluation without consuming a sample and ignores new evaluation requests while busy. Messages travel in either direction between the center and a worker. A payload of m≥0 bits carries an additional 64 zero bits, so its transmission takes ℓ+b(m+64) time, with latency ℓ≥0 and time per bit b≥0. The recipient receives the sender’s identity and the transmitted bits. Each directed link carries one message at a time and ignores submissions while occupied. Distinct directed links can operate concurrently with one another and with worker computations.

The algorithm receives d,n,Ω with its measurable structure, (hi)i=1n,ℓ,b,(Li)i=1n,μ,ρ,R,σ,ε, and x0. For an elapsed-time budget T≥0, almost surely the protocol must finish processing events in finitely many steps at every deadline t∈[0,T]. At time T, the algorithm’s designated output node must produce a measurable x¯∈Rd with integrable squared distance to S satisfying E[dist(x¯,S)2]≤ε, where the expectation is over the algorithm’s randomness and the workers’ samples.

comparisonHtml:
On Rd, each fi is convex with public gradient Lipschitz bound Li. The mean F=n−1∑ifi is L¯-smooth and satisfies F(x)−minF≥(μ/2)dist(x,X∗)2 and n−1∑i∥∇fi(x)∥2≤ρ∥∇F(x)∥2, with μ>0 and ρ≥1. A minimizer lies within R of x0. Jointly measurable worker gradients are unbiased with variance at most σ2, with IID samples within workers and independence across workers. In the finite-bit coordinator star, each worker handles one gradient at a time in hi>0 time and each directed link handles one packet at a time at latency ℓ and cost b per bit. Distinct workers and directed links can run concurrently. The target is Edist(X,X∗)2≤ε for the returned point.

import LongTails.Setups.DistributedMeanStrongGrowth

open DistributedTemplate

namespace LongTails.Setups.DistributedLocallySmoothGrowth

structure Params extends DistributedWeakInterpolation.Params where
  ρ : ℝ

noncomputable abbrev aggregate (p : Params) : DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.Params where
  d := p.d
  n := p.n
  Ω := p.Ω
  h := p.h
  l := p.l
  b := p.b
  L := max p.μ (Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty p.L)
  μ := p.μ
  ρ := p.ρ
  R := p.R
  σ := p.σ
  ε := p.ε
  x0 := p.x0

abbrev Point (p : Params) := DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.Point (aggregate p)
abbrev Functions (p : Params) := DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.Functions (aggregate p)
abbrev Samples (p : Params) := DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.Samples (aggregate p)

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  publicInput := id
  numWorkers p := p.n + 1
  Instance := Functions
  ComputeQuery p := DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.spec.ComputeQuery (aggregate p)
  ComputeReply p := DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.spec.ComputeReply (aggregate p)
  CommReply p := DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.spec.CommReply (aggregate p)
  Output := Point
  valid p := DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.spec.valid (aggregate p) ∧ ∀ i, 0 ≤ p.L i
  admissible p f O := DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.spec.admissible (aggregate p) f O ∧
    ∀ i x y, ‖gradient (f i) x - gradient (f i) y‖ ≤ p.L i * ‖x-y‖
  successful p := DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.spec.successful (aggregate p)

end LongTails.Setups.DistributedLocallySmoothGrowth
